title: Entanglement Cost of Optimal Distributed Quantum State Purification
authors: Jiayi Zhao, Chengkai Zhu, Xin Wang, Ge Bai
abstract: We determine the preshared entanglement required for spatially separated parties, restricted to local operations and classical communication, to attain globally optimal probabilistic two-copy purification of arbitrary bipartite pure states under depolarizing noise. In every local dimension $d\ge 2$, one shared maximally entangled qubit pair suffices: local controlled-SWAP operations exactly reproduce the globally optimal successful transformation. Conversely, any finite-dimensional preshared resource state that attains the same benchmark, even under a positive-partial-transpose relaxation, must have entanglement of formation at least one ebit. For pure resources with one ebit, or for two-qubit resources including mixed states, attaining the benchmark is possible only for states with exactly two nonzero Schmidt weights, both equal to $1/2$, namely those locally unitarily equivalent to a maximally entangled qubit pair. These findings provide a benchmark for evaluating the entanglement demands of noise management in quantum networks and modular quantum computers.
summary: This theoretical paper quantifies the minimum entanglement resource needed for distributed quantum state purification under noise. It proves that for the optimal two-copy purification task, one shared EPR pair is both sufficient and necessary for local operations and classical communication (LOCC) to match the global optimum. This establishes a crucial benchmark for assessing entanglement demands in quantum networking.
main_problem: The paper determines the minimum preshared entanglement required for spatially separated parties to achieve the globally optimal probabilistic two-copy purification of arbitrary bipartite pure states under depolarizing noise.
main_result: For the optimal purification benchmark, one shared maximally entangled qubit pair (EPR pair) suffices for LOCC protocols, and conversely, any resource achieving this optimum must possess at least one ebit of entanglement.
method: The authors use rigorous information-theoretic bounds, comparing achievable LOCC protocols against the optimal global CPTN benchmark, and employing entanglement measures like Entanglement of Formation.
model_or_system: The model involves two spatially separated parties (Alice and Bob) purifying two noisy copies of an arbitrary bipartite pure state ($\psi$) that has undergone independent depolarizing noise. The resource is a finite-dimensional shared entangled state.
key_observables: Quantum fidelity, Entanglement of Formation (EF), and the achievable purification gain relative to the global optimum $G^\star(D, \gamma)$.
important_parameters: Noise strength ($\gamma$), local dimension ($d \ge 2$), and the number of copies ($n=2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to LOCC protocols and focuses on the $2 	o 1$ purification task under depolarizing noise.
figures_summary: Figure 2 illustrates a specific LOCC protocol using an EPR pair involving controlled swaps and a measurement acceptance condition.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by defining the purification task and the benchmark. It then proves the sufficiency of one EPR pair for LOCC to match the global optimum, and subsequently proves the necessity by establishing the minimum entanglement cost using entanglement measures and PPT tests.
why_interesting: This work provides a fundamental, quantitative benchmark for resource requirements in quantum communication and quantum computation, directly impacting the design of quantum network protocols and modular quantum computers.
